cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Security Token Assignment
sites_touched_JUDGEMENT: 14 source files: ApplyPublicOnly added to six query-option types in models/, applied in org, repo, issue, star, watch and user API handlers, plus the repo assignment and API context
sibling_sites_exist_JUDGEMENT: yes: every API listing that can return private organisations, repositories, stars, watches, feeds or users
entry_point_GUESS: HTTP API: GET /api/v1/user/orgs and /api/v1/users/{username}/orgs/{org}/permissions (and other listings) with a personal access token restricted to public-only
services_GUESS: database (built-in SQLite should do; GUESS) and git
flaw_one_line: A personal access token limited to public-only can still read private organisation membership and permissions, because the public-only restriction is enforced by route middleware that is missing on some routes and checks the wrong object on others.
tempting_wrong_fix_JUDGEMENT: Add the existing checkTokenPublicOnly() middleware to the two routes named in the advisory. It evaluates the user in the path rather than the organisations returned, and the starred, watched, feed and search listings stay unfiltered.
why_hard_or_why_control_JUDGEMENT: S1: one restriction must hold in every query that can return private data (the fix touches 14 files). S3: a middleware for exactly this restriction exists and is attached to most routes, so the code looks protected. S2: the fix moves the decision from the route layer to the query options in the model layer. Go, authorisation class.
caveats: 1 referenced fix commits not fetched (cap); Two fix commits referenced; the linked one is dated 2026-05-18, before the June window (the advisory was published 2026-07-21). Large application; build time not measured.
